01
Foundation

The best minutes of every podcast.

Briefly finds the moments in long-form podcasts that are worth hearing and delivers them as short, real audio clips, in the host's own voice, with a path back to the full episode.

We don't rewrite conversations. We find the part you'd want to hear and hand you the play button.

Mission

Make the best ideas in podcasts easy to find, easy to hear, and easy to come back to.

Vision

No great conversation lost inside a three-hour runtime. Every idea worth hearing, one tap away.

What we stand for

Four values. Every product and brand decision should be able to point to at least one of them.

01

Respect for time

Every minute matters. We lead with the moment, cut the filler, and never pad a brief to look bigger than it is.

02

Real voices first

You hear the host, not a summary of the host. We clip, we never rewrite, and the original episode is always one tap away.

03

Creators are partners

Shows bring the ideas. We send listeners back to them, keep their links intact, and build revenue with them, not around them.

04

Curiosity that compounds

One great clip leads to the next show, the next topic, the next idea. We design for the second listen, not just the first.

What changed in 2.0

Edition 1.0 described Briefly as a summary and insights product. The product now delivers real audio, so the language moved with it.

Edition 1.0 said

  • Concise summaries and key insights
  • Transforming conversations into knowledge
  • Curated takeaways to read
  • Podcast intelligence

Edition 2.0 says

  • Short, real audio clips called briefs
  • The moment, in the host's own voice
  • Something you hear, then follow back to the episode
  • Clip-first podcast discovery

Voice and language

Sound like the friend who sends the good part.

Briefly talks the way a well-read friend texts you a timestamp: specific, warm, and quick to get out of the way so the clip can do the talking.

Our words

A shared vocabulary keeps the app, the socials, and the pitch telling one story.

SayInstead ofWhy
BriefSummary, recap, snippetA brief is a real audio clip from an episode. It is never a written rewrite.
Cue a showSubscribe, follow a showCue is our verb for adding a show. Follow is reserved for people.
ListenersUsers, consumers, audiencePeople come to Briefly to listen. Name them for what they do.
Hosts and creatorsContent creators, sourcesThey are people with shows, not a content supply.
Moments, ideasContent, assetsWe sell the idea inside the clip, not volume.
In the host's own voiceAI-generated, AI voiceThe audio is real. Say so, and never imply it was synthesized.
Full episodeLong-form contentPoint to the thing people can actually press play on.
The HiveGrid, tilesThe name of the honeycomb discovery grid on Home.

Voice checker

Paste any line of copy. The checker flags words that pull us off-voice and suggests the Briefly word.

Your copyEdit freely
On-voice check

    Writing rules

    1. Lead with the idea. Say what the clip is about before you say who said it.
    2. Name the show. Credit hosts by show name every time a brief is promoted.
    3. Use numerals. "4 minutes", "3 shows". Numbers are faster to scan.
    4. Sentence case. Headlines and buttons use sentence case, not Title Case.
    5. One exclamation mark per screen, and usually zero.
    6. No em dashes. Use a comma, a colon, or a new sentence.
    7. Short buttons. Two or three words, starting with a verb: "Play brief", "Cue show".
    8. Never overclaim. We help people find ideas. We don't promise to make anyone smarter.

    Logo

    One ghost, one wordmark, no edits.

    The primary mark pairs the listening ghost with the Briefly wordmark and the tagline. It is the single most recognizable thing we own, so it is never redrawn, recolored, or rearranged.

    B
    420px · clear

    Space and size

    The height of the "B" sets the exclusion zone on every side. Below the minimum, the tagline stops being legible.

    Clear space1 × B

    Measured from the cap height of the B in the wordmark.

    Minimum, primary mark100px

    Width of the full lockup on screen. About 25 mm in print.

    Minimum, ghost alone50px

    For favicons, avatars, and tight UI. Below this, use the favicon.

    Don't

    Every one of these breaks recognition. If it isn't one of the five variants above, it isn't the logo.

    06
    Gradients

    Earned, not everywhere.

    The signature gradient is our loudest asset, so we ration it. It lives on the ghost and appears at the payoff: the primary action, the cover, the hero. Explanatory surfaces stay flat.

    Primary · Linear

    Where it goes

    01The ghost mark, always
    02Cover pages and hero sections
    03The one primary action on a screen
    04Social covers and campaign graphics

    Where it doesn't

    01Behind body text or dense reading
    02On more than one button per screen
    03In new stop orders or new colors
    04Under heavy glow, noise, or shadow

    Typography

    A distinct voice up top. Pure clarity below.

    08
    Iconography

    Soft, chunky, friendly.

    Our icons are rounded and generous, drawn on a 48 unit grid with a 3 unit stroke, so they feel as approachable as the ghost. A small sample is shown here.

    States

    Inactive icons sit in muted ink. The active tab picks up violet. Try the tab bar.

    Rules

    One style per surfaceLine icons for navigation and actions. Never mix in other icon styles.
    Never gradient-filledThe gradient belongs to the ghost. Icons stay a single flat color.
    Label what mattersNavigation icons always carry a text label underneath.
